overviewHtml:
Short Introduction

Every year on the full moon of the Nepali month of Baisakh, Lumbini fills with monks, pilgrims and prayer flags to mark the birth, enlightenment and passing of Siddhartha Gautama. Known in Nepal as Buddha Jayanti and across the Buddhist world as Vesak Day, it is the most sacred day of the Buddhist calendar, and Lumbini is where it began.

This 6-day private tour takes you from the stupas of Kathmandu to the Sacred Garden in Lumbini, with a local guide, comfortable transfers and time at the birthplace on the festival day itself.

Buddha Jayanti 2027: Date & Festival Information

  • Expected date: Thursday, 20 May 2027 (Baisakh Purnima, full moon)
  • Occasion: 2,571st birth anniversary of Lord Buddha, according to the Nepali count
  • Also known as: Vesak, Vesakha, Buddha Purnima
  • Public holiday: Yes, across Nepal

Because the festival follows the lunar calendar, the exact date can shift by a day. We confirm it against the official Nepali calendar before finalizing your itinerary, and we build in flexibility so you are in Lumbini when the main ceremonies take place.

Tour Facts

Duration6 days / 5 nights
DestinationsKathmandu & Lumbini
Tour typePrivate tour
PriceFrom US$695 per person
Best forPilgrims, culture lovers, first-time visitors to Nepal, solo travelers, families
TransportPrivate vehicle and domestic flight

Why Experience Buddha Jayanti in Lumbini?

Lumbini is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the place where Queen Mayadevi gave birth to the Buddha. Visiting on Buddha Jayanti means seeing it at its most alive.

  • Walk where the Buddha was born. The Maya Devi Temple, the sacred pond and the Ashoka Pillar mark the exact setting of the birth.
  • See living Buddhism from many traditions. Monks and nuns from Nepal, Tibet, Thailand, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Korea and beyond gather here.
  • Join something rarely seen elsewhere. Chanting, processions, butter lamps, flower offerings and meditation fill the grounds.
  • Travel privately. Your guide handles timing, crowds and logistics so you can focus on the experience.
  • Combine culture and calm. Lumbini's gardens and monastic zone are peaceful, a contrast to Kathmandu's energy.

What Happens During Buddha Jayanti in Lumbini?

Celebrations begin before dawn and continue well into the night:

  • Early morning prayers at the Maya Devi Temple, where pilgrims queue to pay respects at the birthplace.
  • Chanting and puja led by monks at monasteries across the Monastic Zone.
  • Processions of monks, devotees and cultural groups, often with music and traditional dress.
  • Offerings, including flowers, incense, butter lamps and food for the monastic community.
  • Meditation sessions and Dharma talks, often open to visitors.
  • Evening lamp lighting around the sacred pond and monasteries.

Dress modestly, expect crowds, and be ready for a long day. Your guide will suggest the best times to enter the main sites and the quieter moments for reflection.

5 Night, 6 Days Buddha Jayanti Tour Itinerary

Day 1: Kathmandu Arrival 1400 m

Upon your arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu, a representative from Nepal Unique Treks Tour Agency will warmly welcome you outside the arrival terminal. You will then be transferred to your hotel in a private tourist vehicle.

After checking into your hotel, take some time to relax and recover from your international journey. Later, our tour representative will provide a short briefing about the 5 Night, 6 days Buddhist pilgrimage tour, including the travel arrangements, important Buddhist heritage sites and the upcoming Buddha Jayanti celebrations in Lumbini.

If you arrive early and feel comfortable exploring, you can enjoy an optional evening walk around Thamel, one of Kathmandu's popular tourist areas. You can explore local handicraft shops, Buddhist souvenirs, prayer flags, singing bowls and traditional Nepali restaurants.

Return to your hotel and enjoy your first overnight stay in Kathmandu.

Overnight: Hotel in Kathmandu.

Day 2: Kathmandu Buddhist Heritage Tour

After breakfast, meet your experienced English-speaking tour guide and begin a full-day exploration of Kathmandu Valley's most important Buddhist heritage sites. Kathmandu is an ancient centre of Buddhist culture, where Tibetan Buddhist traditions and Newar Buddhism have flourished for centuries.

1. Swayambhunath Stupa (Monkey Temple)

Begin your pilgrimage at Swayambhunath, one of the oldest and most sacred Buddhist stupas in Nepal. Located on a beautiful hilltop overlooking Kathmandu Valley, this UNESCO World Heritage Site offers panoramic views of the city.

Explore the white dome, golden spire, colourful prayer flags and the famous Buddha eyes painted on the four sides of the stupa. You can observe local Buddhist devotees and monks performing prayers, spinning prayer wheels and walking clockwise around the sacred monument.

2. Boudhanath Stupa

Continue to Boudhanath Stupa, one of the largest spherical stupas in the world and an important centre of Tibetan Buddhism outside Tibet.

Walk around the enormous white dome while observing pilgrims performing kora (clockwise circumambulation), monks chanting prayers and devotees spinning prayer wheels. Explore the surrounding Tibetan monasteries, traditional shops and Buddhist cultural centres.

You may also visit a monastery and experience the peaceful atmosphere of Buddhist prayer and meditation.

3. Patan Durbar Square and Golden Temple

In the afternoon, visit the historic city of Patan, famous for its traditional Newari architecture, Buddhist monasteries and ancient craftsmanship.

Explore Patan Durbar Square and visit Hiranya Varna Mahavihar, popularly known as the Golden Temple. This beautiful Buddhist monastery is decorated with intricate metalwork, traditional sculptures and religious artwork.

Discover the connection between Newar Buddhist culture, local traditions and the everyday spiritual life of the people. After completing the sightseeing tour, return to your hotel and enjoy a relaxing evening.

Overnight: Hotel in Kathmandu.

Day 3: Fly to Bhairahawa & Transfer to Lumbini

After an early breakfast, transfer to Kathmandu Domestic Airport for your scenic flight to Gautam Buddha International Airport in Bhairahawa. The flight takes approximately 30/40 minutes, depending on flight operations and weather conditions.

Upon arrival in Bhairahawa, our representative and driver will welcome you and arrange a private vehicle transfer to Lumbini, approximately 30/40 minutes away.

Lumbini is one of the world's most important Buddhist pilgrimage destinations and is recognised as the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama, Lord Buddha. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site visited by Buddhist pilgrims from different countries, particularly Nepal, India, Vietnam, Thailand, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, China, Japan and South Korea.

After arriving in Lumbini, check into your hotel and enjoy some time to rest. In the afternoon, begin exploring the peaceful Lumbini Sacred Garden and surrounding Monastic Zone, depending on the day's schedule and access arrangements.

You can visit the Lumbini Museum to learn about the life of Buddha, the history of Buddhism and the archaeological discoveries associated with Lumbini. Explore the international monasteries representing different Buddhist countries and traditions.

In the evening, enjoy a peaceful walk through the monastery area, observe Buddhist pilgrims arriving for Buddha Jayanti and experience the spiritual atmosphere before the main celebration. Return to your hotel for dinner and overnight accommodation.

Overnight: Hotel in Lumbini.

Day 4: Buddha Jayanti Celebration & Lumbini

Today is the most important day of your Buddhist pilgrimage journey. Celebrate Buddha Jayanti at Lumbini, the sacred birthplace of Lord Buddha, together with thousands of Buddhist devotees, monks, nuns and international pilgrims.

Buddha Jayanti commemorates the birth, enlightenment and Mahaparinirvana of Gautama Buddha. The celebration provides a wonderful opportunity to experience Buddhist devotion, traditional ceremonies and international spiritual gatherings.

1. Maya Devi Temple - Sacred Birthplace of Buddha

Start early with a visit to Maya Devi Temple, the most sacred monument in Lumbini. This temple marks the exact location traditionally recognised as the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama. Explore the archaeological remains, sacred marker stone and nativity sculpture depicting Queen Maya Devi giving birth to Siddhartha Gautama. Spend some peaceful moments in prayer, meditation and reflection.

2. Ashoka Pillar

Visit the historic Ashoka Pillar, erected by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BCE during his pilgrimage to Lumbini. The inscription on the pillar provides important historical evidence identifying Lumbini as the birthplace of Lord Buddha. This is one of the most significant historical monuments for Buddhist pilgrims and historians.

3. Puskarini Sacred Pond

Continue to Puskarini Pond, traditionally associated with the sacred events surrounding Buddha's birth. According to Buddhist tradition, Queen Maya Devi bathed in this pond before giving birth to Siddhartha Gautama. Enjoy the peaceful surroundings and learn about the religious significance of this important pilgrimage site.

4. International Monastic Zone

Explore the East and West Monastic Zones, where Buddhist countries have established monasteries representing their unique architectural styles and religious traditions. You can visit monasteries associated with countries such as Thailand, Myanmar, Cambodia, Vietnam, China, Japan, South Korea, Germany and France, depending on access and opening arrangements.

Observe monks and devotees participating in prayers, meditation, chanting and religious ceremonies.

5. World Peace Pagoda

Visit the beautiful World Peace Pagoda, built as a symbol of peace, harmony and universal brotherhood. Its peaceful surroundings provide an ideal place for reflection, photography and spiritual contemplation.

6. Evening Buddha Jayanti Celebration

In the evening, experience the special Buddha Jayanti atmosphere throughout Lumbini. Depending on the official festival programme, you may witness religious processions, prayer ceremonies, Buddhist chanting, cultural performances and the lighting of butter lamps or other devotional lights. Join local and international pilgrims in offering prayers and celebrating the life and teachings of Lord Buddha. Return to your hotel after this memorable spiritual experience.

Overnight: Hotel in Lumbini.

Day 5: Flight from Lumbini to Kathmandu

After breakfast, enjoy another opportunity to explore the historical heritage associated with the early life of Siddhartha Gautama.

Drive to Tilaurakot, the archaeological site traditionally identified as the ancient capital of the Shakya Kingdom. According to Buddhist tradition, Siddhartha Gautama spent his early years in the Shakya royal family before renouncing worldly life in search of enlightenment.

Explore the archaeological remains of the ancient city, including its historic fortifications, gateways and excavated structures. Your guide will explain the historical and religious significance of the site and its connection with the Buddha's early life.

After sightseeing, return to Bhairahawa and transfer to Gautam Buddha International Airport for your domestic flight back to Kathmandu.

Upon arrival in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you to your hotel. Enjoy a relaxed evening. You may explore local markets, purchase Buddhist souvenirs, prayer flags, singing bowls, handmade crafts and traditional Nepali gifts for your family and friends.

Overnight: Hotel in Kathmandu.

Day 6: Departure

After breakfast, enjoy your final morning in Nepal. Depending on your international flight schedule, you may have some free time for shopping or relaxing at your hotel.

Our Nepal Unique Treks representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport by private vehicle at least three hours before your international flight departure.

We hope your Buddhist pilgrimage journey has provided beautiful memories, spiritual inspiration and a deeper understanding of the life and teachings of Lord Buddha. Thank you for travelling with Nepal Unique Treks . We look forward to welcoming you again for another memorable journey in Nepal.

Top Places to Visit in Lumbini

  • Maya Devi Temple: Built over the spot where the Buddha is believed to have been born, with ancient brick foundations preserved inside.
  • Ashoka Pillar: Erected by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BCE, with an inscription recognizing Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace.
  • Puskarini Pond: The sacred pool where Queen Mayadevi is said to have bathed before the birth.
  • Monastic Zone: Dozens of monasteries built by Buddhist communities from around the world, split into Theravada (East) and Mahayana/Vajrayana (West) zones.
  • World Peace Pagoda: A white stupa built by Japanese Buddhists.
  • Lumbini Museum: Artifacts and exhibits on Buddhist history and the region.
  • Lumbini Crane Sanctuary: A peaceful reserve known for the Sarus crane.
  • Tilaurakot, Gotihawa, Niglihawa and Ramagrama: Archaeological sites nearby connected to the Buddha's life and the wider Buddhist circuit.

How to Reach Lumbini

  • By air (recommended): Fly from Kathmandu to Gautam Buddha Airport in Bhairahawa, then drive about 30–40 minutes to Lumbini.
  • By road: The drive from Kathmandu takes around 8–9 hours depending on traffic and conditions. From Pokhara, it takes about 6–7 hours.
  • From India: Lumbini is a short drive from the Sunauli border, near Gorakhpur and Varanasi.

On a festival week, flights fill up and roads get busy. This is a good reason to book early and travel with a private operator.

Best Time to Visit Lumbini for Vesak

  • Festival timing: Buddha Jayanti falls in late April or May, and in 2027 is expected on 20 May.
  • Weather: Lumbini is in the Terai lowlands, so it is hot in May, often 35–40°C. Plan outdoor visits for early morning and late afternoon.
  • Off-festival alternatives: October to March has cooler, more comfortable weather but no Vesak celebrations.

If you want the festival atmosphere, May is the month. If you prefer comfort over ceremony, consider the cooler season.

Buddha Jayanti Travel Tips

  • Book early. Flights and hotels in Lumbini sell out around the festival.
  • Dress modestly. Cover shoulders and knees, and remove shoes and hats at temples.
  • Beat the heat. Carry water, sunscreen, a hat and light cotton clothing.
  • Start early. The most peaceful hours at the sacred sites are at dawn.
  • Be respectful. Ask before photographing monks or worshippers, and do not touch sacred objects.
  • Carry small cash. Useful for offerings, donations and small purchases.
  • Walk clockwise around stupas and prayer wheels.
  • Plan for crowds. Be patient, since the festival draws large numbers of pilgrims.

Tour Cost for 2027

Because Buddha Jayanti is a peak period, we recommend booking several months ahead to secure the best rates and rooms. Contact us for a customized quote, including upgrades, extra days or add-ons such as Pokhara or Chitwan.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Valley sightseeing 1345 m, 5 hrs
itinerary.description: Kathmandu Valley is a cultural and historical hub of Nepal and home to several UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Here's a suggested itinerary for Kathmandu Valley sightseeing: Kathmandu Durbar Square is home to several historical palaces, temples, and courtyards. See the intricate carvings on the wooden windows and doors of the old buildings and take in the beauty of the Hanuman Dhoka Palace, Taleju Temple, and the Kumari Ghar (home to the Living Goddess). Swayambhunath Stupa, also known as the Monkey Temple, sits atop a hill overlooking Kathmandu. Explore the colorful temples, prayer flags, and Buddhist shrines that surround the stupa, and take in the stunning panoramic views of the city. Boudhanath Stupa is one of the largest stupas in the world and a significant pilgrimage site for Tibetan Buddhists. Walk around the stupa, spin the prayer wheels, and observe the devotees performing their rituals.

liveFaqs.question: When is Buddha Jayanti in 2027?
liveFaqs.answer: It is expected on 20 May 2027, the full moon day of Baisakh. We confirm the exact date against the official calendar.

liveFaqs.question: Is Lumbini crowded during Buddha Jayanti?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes, it is busy, especially at the Maya Devi Temple. Early starts and a private guide help you avoid the worst of the crowds.

liveFaqs.question: Is this tour suitable for non-Buddhists?
liveFaqs.answer: Absolutely. The tour suits anyone interested in culture, history, spirituality or travel.

liveFaqs.question: How hot is Lumbini in May?
liveFaqs.answer: Very hot, often above 35°C. Wear light clothing, drink plenty of water and plan outdoor visits for the morning and evening.

liveFaqs.question: Can the tour be customized?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. We can add days, upgrade hotels, include Pokhara or Chitwan, or adjust the pace.

liveFaqs.question: Do I need a visa for Nepal?
liveFaqs.answer: Most visitors need one. You can usually get a tourist visa on arrival or apply online in advance. Check current rules before you travel.

liveFaqs.question: What should I wear?
liveFaqs.answer: Modest, lightweight clothing that covers shoulders and knees, plus comfortable shoes that are easy to remove.

liveFaqs.question: Is it safe for solo travelers and families?
liveFaqs.answer: Yes. The itinerary is easy, and we provide a guide and driver throughout.

liveFaqs.question: Can I join the ceremonies?
liveFaqs.answer: Visitors are welcome to observe and, in many cases, join quiet prayers or meditation. Your guide will explain etiquette.
